title: Nucleus, endplate and whole disc
summary: Simulate nucleus torsional shear, confined compression and swelling of NP/AF/endplate plugs, and whole-disc compression, shear and internal strain.
simulate: Build each specimen at its stated size: NP cylinder (8 mm), confined plug (4-5 mm), or disc with vertebral bodies.
Use the stated bath (0.15 M saline/PBS) and let the tissue swell to equilibrium before loading where stated.
Torsion: 10% axial offset, sinusoidal or ramp-hold twist. Confined compression: porous platen, ramp-hold steps to equilibrium.
Whole disc: fix the lower vertebra; apply the stated compression, shear or rotation with preload and rate as given.
Report the output as defined (|G*|, phase angle, fitted or equivalent Ha/k0, swelling stress or ratio, stiffness, strain).

outputs.label: Axial tangent stiffness at peak load

notes: Aggregate modulus and permeability are per-sample fits; Cortes biphasic and biphasic-swelling fits and Iatridis finite-deformation fits are separate tasks. Compare by fitting your model, or by reproducing the relaxation curves.
Confined compression of AF sits here (not in annulus_tissue). Endplate = Cortes 2014 cartilaginous endplate only. Skrzypiec motion segments and other segment stiffness are in segment_stiffness.

Left out (in bench/tests): Cortes E, nu, beta, M, FCD, GAG, water; Iatridis 1998 beta and M; Iatridis 1997b water; Galante water content; Jamison 0.2/0.8 mm rate curves; Costi physiological (extrapolated) strains.
agent_prompt: You are given a constitutive or finite element model of human lumbar disc tissue (nucleus, annulus, cartilaginous endplate) or of a whole disc. For every task, build the specimen in its inputs (tissue, region, test mode, degeneration) and simulate the test: torsional shear of an NP cylinder at the given frequency or ramp-hold, confined compression with a porous platen and the stated bath, free or confined swelling, or whole-disc compression, shear and rotation with the stated preload, displacement and duration. Report the output exactly as defined; for fitted parameters (aggregate modulus, k0) fit the named model to your simulated response or report your equivalent parameter. Use one parameter set per tissue. Return one JSON object following answer_format (task id -> {output key: value}); use null when not simulated.
